s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic skin condition with multiple whitish papules and pruritic lesions on the trunk
salient_findings: Numerous whitish papules on the back of more than 10 years' duration
Papules became pruritic and extended to the waist and anterior trunk
Folliculocentric papules with central keratin plugs and surrounding erythema
key_facts: Woman in her 60s
Lesions previously resolved with topical corticosteroids
Lesions flared soon after treatment discontinuation
No family history of similar lesions
Multiple hypopigmented, flat-topped papules on the back, waist, and inframammary area
Most lesions were folliculocentric
Dermoscopy revealed central keratin plugs and structureless, whitish, and homogenous areas
Antinuclear antibody and hyperglobulinemia tests were negative
Biopsy specimen showed central follicular plug and epidermal atrophy
Papillary dermis was markedly thickened with homogenized collagens and sparse bandlike lymphocytic infiltration

shortlist.label: Keratosis Pilaris
shortlist.why_kept: Folliculocentric papules and central keratin plugs on dermoscopy

shortlist.label: Lichen Spinulosus
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple hypopigmented, flat-topped papules and pruritic lesions

shortlist.label: Keratosis Follicularis
shortlist.why_kept: Central follicular plug and epidermal atrophy on histopathology

shortlist.label: Grover Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Pruritic papules and histopathological findings of epidermal atrophy

shortlist.label: Darier Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Keratotic papules and histopathological findings of suprabasal acantholysis

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple hypopigmented, flat-topped, and folliculocentric papules, along with dermoscopic findings of central keratin plugs and structureless, whitish, and homogenous areas, are characteristic of Lichen Spinulosus. The biopsy specimen showing central follicular plug and epidermal atrophy also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Keratosis Pilaris
rejected.why: While Keratosis Pilaris can present with folliculocentric papules, it typically lacks the flat-topped and hypopigmented characteristics seen in this case.

rejected.label: Keratosis Follicularis
rejected.why: Keratosis Follicularis is not a recognized dermatological condition, suggesting it may be a distractor.

rejected.label: Grover Disease
rejected.why: Grover Disease typically presents with sudden onset of multiple, discrete, and pruritic papules, which does not fully align with the long-standing nature of the lesions in this case.

rejected.label: Darier Disease
rejected.why: Darier Disease is characterized by greasy, crusted, or verrucous papules, which differs significantly from the hypopigmented and flat-topped papules described.
